name: Squash
grown_as: A winter squash grown as a tender annual: sown under cover in late spring, planted out after frost, the fruit stored for winter. Varieties differ most in fruit: drawn as an orange onion-shaped squash like 'Uchiki Kuri'; 'Crown Prince' is blue-grey. Butternut squash is a different species (Cucurbita moschata) with a five-angled stalk and a pear-shaped buff fruit. ⚠️ CHECK which squash William grows.
habit: A long trailing vine, 3 to 5 m, running along the ground and rooting at its joints, with branched tendrils that grip anything nearby. Leaves stand up on long stalks above the vine, making a carpet 40 to 60 cm deep. Stems are round, soft-hairy and not prickly.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate along the running vine, one at each joint with a tendril and often a flower
leaf.outline: Nearly round to kidney-shaped, 20 to 35 cm across, unlobed or with five very shallow, rounded lobes
leaf.base: Deeply heart-shaped, the two rounded lobes at the base often close together
leaf.tip: Rounded or with a short blunt point
leaf.margin: Small irregular teeth all round; edge gently wavy
leaf.veins: Palmate: five main veins spreading from the stalk top, with a net of smaller veins
leaf.surface: Soft-hairy, velvety, not prickly; usually no silver blotches
leaf.stalk: Long (20 to 40 cm), round, hollow, soft-hairy

flower.form: A large trumpet, wider and more open than a courgette's
flower.petals: Joined into a funnel splitting into five broad rounded lobes that flare out and curl back
flower.centre: Male: one thick yellow column of joined stamens. Female: a thick lobed orange stigma.
flower.behind: Five narrow green sepals. Female flowers sit on a small round swelling, the young squash.
flower.carried: Singly from the joints of the vine, males on long stalks, females on short stalks, facing up or out

fruit: Large, heavy fruit lying on the ground along the vine, 1 to 5 kg. 'Uchiki Kuri' is teardrop or onion-shaped, 15 to 20 cm, smooth, bright red-orange with faint paler stripes. The fruit stalk is the clue to the species: round, thick, soft and corky, swelling and cracking as it ripens, not ridged. Seeds plump, white to tan, 15 to 25 mm, with a thin pale edge.
seedling: Two large, thick, smooth, oval seed leaves on a stout stem, then a rounded, softly hairy first true leaf with a toothed edge.
winter: Nothing: killed by the first frost. The harvested fruit are stored indoors.

leaf: one big rounded or kidney-shaped leaf, at most shallowly lobed
five main veins spreading from the stalk
bloom: a large yellow-orange trumpet with five broad rounded lobes flared back
a thick column or lobed stigma in the centre
seed: a plump flat oval seed, white to tan
15 to 25 mm, bigger than a courgette seed
seedling: two big smooth oval seed leaves
a small rounded toothed true leaf
young: a vine starting to run along the ground
round leaves standing on long stalks
crop: large orange squash lying on the ground along the vine
round leaves on long stalks above

look_alikes: Courgettes and pumpkins (Cucurbita pepo) have deeply lobed, prickly leaves and a hard five-angled fruit stalk. Butternut (C. moschata) has softer, slightly lobed leaves often with white patches and a five-angled stalk flaring at the fruit.
